n: True happiness belongs to the one whose sin has been forgiven and covered by God. Paul quotes this psalm to teach that forgiveness is a gift of grace.

f.g: Happy, fortunate — the same word that opens Psalm 1.
Hidden from view; atoned for. The Hebrew idea of atonement includes covering sin.

n: Blessed is the person God no longer charges with guilt — and who is honest, without deceit. Forgiveness and honesty go together.

f.g: Does not count or charge against him.

n: David remembers what it was like when he hid his sin: his body felt old and he groaned all day long. Unconfessed sin weighs on the whole person.

f.g: Groaning or crying out in anguish.

n: He felt God’s hand pressing on him day and night, and his strength dried up like plants in summer heat. Conviction of sin can be a merciful pressure.

f.g: A musical or liturgical marker of uncertain meaning, possibly a pause or a lift in the music.

f.w: thy hand was heavy upon me

n: The turning point: “I said, I will confess” — and God forgave. Healing came the moment David stopped hiding. This is a model of repentance.

f.w: I acknowledged my sin unto thee

n: Because of this, every faithful person should pray while God may be found. When floods of trouble come, they won’t sweep him away.

f.w: in a time when thou mayest be found

n: God is a hiding place who surrounds the forgiven person with songs of rescue, like a choir all around.
Now God himself seems to speak: I will teach you the way and keep my eye on you. Guidance follows forgiveness.

f.w: I will guide thee with mine eye
f.g: Possibly “I will counsel you with my eye upon you” — watching over you as you go.

n: Don’t be like a stubborn horse or mule that must be steered with bit and bridle. God wants willing, understanding followers, not ones dragged along.
The wicked face many sorrows, but the one who trusts the Lord is wrapped around by his loyal love.

f.g: God’s ḥesed (steadfast love) will surround him.

n: The psalm ends in celebration: the forgiven and upright should shout for joy. Repentance leads to gladness, not gloom.
